response.markdown_report:
The strongest next experiment remains a **sequence-normalized 0.5 terminal/reconstruction objective mixture**, with a small gradient audit. At 30% progress, prioritize this feasible hypothesis; defer adaptive gradient surgery until harmful interference is demonstrated.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, Electronics has weaker sampled-pair separation, but training margins establish neither cause nor generalization. Second, category identity propagation blocks serving parity; repair the integration before interpreting interventions, without assuming predictions are wrong. Third, equal branch frequencies do not equal target exposure, gradient influence or GPU cost. Different loss reductions also change sequence weighting and require an explicit control.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec [1] combines random-mask and last-only examples; random reconstruction can include the terminal position. RSS [2] motivates examining supervision alignment, without proving conflict. PCGrad [3] motivates gradient-direction measurements; GradNorm [4] motivates magnitude measurements. Replicability findings [5] identify undertraining and efficiency as confounders under a fixed compute budget.

These observations define three directions: serving verification, objective normalization, and interference measurement. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|
| Verification | Reloaded-checkpoint parity | Category identity blocks measurement |
| Alignment | Random reconstruction and terminal masking | Unknown validation benefit and exposure effects |
| Optimization | Gradient cosine, norms and learning curves | Unknown functional transfer and convergence |

Three candidate algorithms follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequence-normalized fixed mixture [1,2,5] | 4/6/5 | Interpretable combination; reusable protocol; unchanged backbone | Established components; uncertain gains; controls and parity add work |
| Equal-norm gradient transfer probe [3,4] | 5/6/6 | Useful functional adaptation; informs mechanisms; no retraining required | Established intervention logic; local effects may not generalize; restoration is delicate |
| PCGrad between objectives [3] | 3/5/6 | Established method; potentially useful against harmful conflict; available gradient APIs | Limited novelty; conflict is unproven; projection and tied parameters complicate implementation |

For the selected mixture, retain baseline user/endpoint sampling and reconstruction corruption. Randomly assign exactly half of each even batch to terminal-only masking. Average target losses within each sequence, then examples within each branch; optimize `0.5*L_terminal + 0.5*L_reconstruction`. This differs from pooling targets within each branch when target counts vary.

```python
for branch in [terminal, reconstruction]:
    examples = baseline_examples_with_fixed_branch_allocation(branch)
    L[branch] = mean(mean(baseline_target_losses(x)) for x in examples)
optimize(0.5 * L[terminal] + 0.5 * L[reconstruction])
```

Compare reconstruction-only, terminal-only and mixture arms with identical sequence reduction, initialization and update schedules, subject to a preregistered budget. Preserve the corrected baseline’s actual sampler rather than importing either paper’s defaults. Log exposure, target counts, reductions, updates and GPU seconds; equal updates do not isolate objective effects. Audit frozen paired gradients descriptively, including tied-parameter deduplication and undefined zero-norm cases.

Preserve one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, synchronized serving interfaces, appended MASK, actual final nonpadding readout, fixed seeds and training limits. Predeclare host evaluation intervals and selection ties. Select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Report final-update performance only if available through the authorized host protocol. No gain, recovered intent or full-catalog benefit is demonstrated; repeated validation selection remains optimistic.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02257; [5] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483.

idea.description: Test a preregistered 0.5 terminal/reconstruction mixture in the corrected BERT4Rec backbone, using per-sequence target means and equal branch coefficients. Compare with reconstruction-only and terminal-only controls under the same reduction and update schedule, within a fixed total budget. Use a small paired gradient audit to distinguish nominal weighting from actual optimization influence.
idea.motivation: Appended-mask serving and random masked reconstruction provide different contexts and supervision positions, but no supplied evidence establishes harmful objective conflict. The original BERT4Rec already includes last-only examples, so novelty concerns the controlled weighting experiment rather than introducing terminal supervision. Existing training margins and qualitative feedback motivate a hypothesis; they do not demonstrate a cause, user intent or validation benefit. Replicability findings make learning trajectories and compute accounting necessary before attributing results to objective composition.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the corrected family-specific baseline architecture, target loss, negative sampler, user sampling and endpoint policy. Before implementation, specify the host sampler's actual endpoint distribution, window construction, masking density, count cap, rounding, replacement policy and treatment of the terminal position. The supplied evidence does not expose all those values; inherit them from the corrected baseline and serialize them into the trial configuration. Do not substitute original BERT4Rec sliding windows or Petrov–Macdonald latest-window sampling. Reconstruction must not be described as interior-only unless the actual host policy excludes the last position.

Use a common sampled training window ending at endpoint t for both branch definitions. Terminal-only input contains the preceding history, truncated to maxlen-1, followed by reserved MASK; supervise only interaction t and include no later interactions. Reconstruction uses the corrected baseline's window and selected-target policy, including its terminal-position eligibility. Every selected target follows the supplied all-MASK corruption policy. An interior reconstruction target can have visible context on both sides; this legitimate reconstruction context must not become shifted future-target leakage. Require nonempty supervision and record any sampler retries. If the existing baseline does not provide common endpoint/window construction, document the difference rather than claiming a fully matched comparison.

For an even batch size B, assign exactly B/2 examples to each mixture branch using a dedicated deterministic generator. Define l_i=(1/m_i)*sum_j loss_ij over the m_i supervised positions of sequence i. Define L_branch as the mean of l_i over that branch and L_mix=0.5*L_terminal+0.5*L_reconstruction. Equal branch sizes make this equivalent to averaging all sequence means. Pooling all targets within each branch is a different estimator when m_i varies; pooling targets across the entire mixed batch additionally changes effective branch weighting. Summing target losses before averaging sequences changes gradient scale. Record the exact baseline reduction and do not silently replace it. Equal coefficients establish neither equal target exposure nor equal gradient influence.

Preregister three fresh-training arms: reconstruction-only, terminal-only and the fixed mixture. All use the same per-sequence reduction, architecture, initialization seed, batch size, optimizer, update schedule and allowed epochs. Use dedicated random streams for common example sampling, branch allocation, corruption and negative sampling so branch-specific random consumption does not unnecessarily change subsequent sampled users/endpoints. Different input corruption and dropout consumption can still produce different training paths. Each arm trains one independent BERT4Rec per category; never reuse another trial's checkpoint or fuse predictions. If the original corrected-baseline reduction differs, report its existing result as context only: comparison with that baseline conflates composition and reduction. A fresh original-reduction control requires a separately budgeted trial.

Allocate the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget before launching arms, including all four categories, diagnostics, debugging and failures. Keep 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs; use a common preregistered feasible update schedule for the arms. If budget requires fewer epochs, choose that common cap beforehand and disclose it. Do not promise all arms to 200 epochs without a runtime estimate. If the full three-arm study cannot fit, prioritize mixture versus reconstruction-only, declare terminal-only unrun, and limit conclusions accordingly. Equal updates and architecture do not guarantee equal GPU cost or supervision exposure; this is an update-controlled, budget-constrained comparison rather than an isolated objective effect. Exposure-matched experiments are additional controls only if budget permits.

Log per category and branch: example and sequence counts, nonpadding input tokens, supervised-target counts and their distribution, loss sums and denominators, optimizer updates, learning rate, GPU seconds and available training/validation trajectories. Count terminal-position supervision occurring inside reconstruction separately from explicit terminal-only examples. Interpret weaker margins cautiously and inspect optimization trajectories; do not infer convergence from positive in-sample margins. Keep the loss and negative-sampling distribution fixed across arms. No popularity predictor, separately fitted transition score or independent expert may supplement neural scores.

On a small fixed, budgeted set of public training windows, compute both objective gradients at identical frozen parameters. Record user/endpoint identities, masks, target positions, negative candidates, checkpoint hash, precision, seeds and software versions. Use model.eval() with autograd enabled, no autocast unless explicitly declared, and autograd.grad without optimizer steps, clipping or adaptive reweighting. Restore model mode and RNG states afterward. Define disjoint parameter blocks and a stable flattening order; count tied item/output embeddings once and include their combined gradient. Retain unused-parameter flags, representing missing gradients as zero entries. Report raw and coefficient-scaled norms, norm ratio, cosine, negative-cosine frequency and zero-norm counts. Declare a numerical zero threshold before measurement; zero-norm cosines and ratios with zero denominators are unavailable, not zero. Distinguish mean batch cosine from cosine of mean gradients. Use paired-batch descriptive intervals, acknowledging shared users/windows and fixed-checkpoint conditioning. Include a diagnostic target-count-matched variant with one reconstruction target sampled under a declared rule; this narrows exposure differences but does not equalize target positions or visible context. The audit remains descriptive and does not trigger PCGrad. Defer equal-norm functional perturbations unless a separately budgeted follow-up is justified.

Repair explicit category identity propagation to ModelView using the actual category from the training loop. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain family-specific sample_batch and loader tensors shaped B x L. Return measured metrics and definitions, explicit denominators and availability. Avoid runtime source introspection for dynamically loaded classes: use the real exported loader and serialized configuration. Verify exact current-checkpoint state identity and finite internal/exported scores with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, plus identical diagnostic rankings on short, full-length, truncated and batched histories. Failed or unavailable parity blocks interpretation of sensitivity and residual patching; it does not itself establish a serving defect. Retain existing embedding, sampled-margin and valid behavioral probes. Restore diagnostic model/RNG state and remove temporary hooks in finally blocks.

Predeclare identical host-approved checkpoint evaluation intervals, the four-category macro validation HR@10 selection rule and deterministic selection ties, such as earliest evaluated update. Select a common arm/checkpoint schedule across categories rather than adaptively assembling category winners from different arms. Each deployed category still loads one selected checkpoint. Do not change the host evaluator or add independent evaluation against unavailable labels. Report the common final-update checkpoint as a supplementary comparison only if the host exposes its evaluation under the existing protocol; otherwise mark it unavailable. If the host exposes paired per-user hits, bootstrap paired users within each category and recompute the four-category macro difference for a descriptive 95% interval. Such intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidate sets, exclude seed variation, and do not correct adaptive checkpoint/search selection. Never reconstruct unavailable per-user outcomes. Label conclusions exploratory and retain failed attempts in the search record.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and trial-local artifacts. Keep checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer synchronized. Serving retains the latest maxlen-1 interactions, appends reserved MASK and reads its actual final nonpadding index, never count-1. PAD and MASK are not recommendation candidates. Each category loads exactly one trained model/checkpoint; no checkpoint averaging or score fusion. Retain five real training users per category receiving full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable review fields, product specifications and simulator traits remain unobserved.

Potential shortcuts include reliance on item frequency, absolute position and recurrent terminal-target patterns. Preserve existing user splits and candidate construction; do not add unsupported adversarial or popularity corrections. Descriptive results by training-history length or training-item frequency can reveal concentration if computed from available data and budgeted beforehand, but cannot prove recovered intent. Sparse qualitative judgments on twenty training users are not validation labels and must not drive item-specific rules. Fixed sampled-candidate HR@10 supports conclusions only for the pinned protocol, not full-catalog ranking. Leave final held-out evaluation to the host.
idea.pseudocode:
preregister arms, reductions, sampler configuration, update cap, budget,
            host evaluation intervals and selection tie rule
arms = [RECONSTRUCTION_ONLY, TERMINAL_ONLY, FIXED_HALF_MIXTURE]
# If budget cannot support all three, declare the reduced comparison before launch.
for arm in scheduled_arms:
    for category in four_required_categories:
        initialize corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42
        create deterministic streams for examples, branches, masks and negatives
        for epoch in range(preregistered_cap_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                windows = sample_corrected_baseline_training_windows()
                branches = arm_specific_labels_with_exact_half_mix_when_applicable()
                example_losses = {TERMINAL: [], RECONSTRUCTION: []}
                for window, branch in zip(windows, branches):
                    if branch == TERMINAL:
                        x, targets = preceding_history_plus_reserved_MASK(window)
                    else:
                        x, targets = corrected_baseline_reconstruction(window)
                    assert nonempty_targets_follow_all_MASK_policy(x, targets)
                    losses = unchanged_baseline_unreduced_target_loss(model(x), targets)
                    example_losses[branch].append(losses.mean())
                    record_examples_tokens_targets_and_reduction_denominators()
                if arm == FIXED_HALF_MIXTURE:
                    loss = 0.5 * mean(example_losses[TERMINAL])
                         + 0.5 * mean(example_losses[RECONSTRUCTION])
                else:
                    loss = mean(example_losses[active_branch])
                optimizer_step(loss)
                record_update_and_compute_cost()
            save_eligible_checkpoint_at_preregistered_intervals()
        save_final_update_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()
        verify_reload_identity_and_exported_serving_parity()
        run_budgeted_paired_gradient_audit_without_parameter_updates()
# Checkpoints within an arm are training snapshots; deploy exactly one per category.
submit_artifacts_through_unchanged_host_validation_protocol()
select_by_preregistered_four_category_macro_HR10_and_tie_rule()
report_exposure_compute_trajectories_failures_and_available_paired_uncertainty()
leave_held_out_evaluation_to_host()

originality.positive: Explicit branch weighting, sequence reduction, exposure accounting and matched controls make an established objective combination scientifically interpretable.
originality.negative: Original BERT4Rec already includes terminal-only examples; a 0.5 mixture and loss normalization introduce no new backbone or optimization principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could establish whether serving-aligned supervision merits further study and support later functional-transfer experiments.
future_potential.negative: Neither the diagnostics nor cited studies demonstrate gains for this mixture, and fixed-budget undertraining or exposure differences can dominate outcomes.

code_difficulty.positive: The training change reuses the corrected encoder, target loss, negative sampler and serving computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible multi-arm sampling, budget allocation, parity repair, tied-parameter gradient accounting and host-limited uncertainty reporting add substantial work beyond changing a loss coefficient.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item prediction.
The original generator combines random-mask copies with a last-only copy; random masking can include the terminal position.
limitations: Does not establish the optimal terminal/reconstruction weighting for this benchmark.
Its released sampling and pooled-target reduction must not be assumed identical to the corrected host baseline.

related_work.title: Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling
contributions: Discusses correspondence between training supervision and next-item recommendation.
Motivates examining training-example construction and recency.
limitations: RSS is a separate sampling method, not a synonym for terminal/interior masking.
Does not validate a 0.5 mixture or establish harmful gradient conflict in this task.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Introduces PCGrad for modifying conflicting task gradients.
Motivates measuring gradient directions before applying conflict-specific interventions.
limitations: Negative cosine alone does not establish harmful functional transfer or validation degradation.
Projection adds complexity and is deferred in the selected experiment.

related_work.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
contributions: Uses gradient magnitudes for adaptive multitask loss balancing.
Supports distinguishing nominal loss coefficients from measured optimization influence.
limitations: Equal gradient norms need not optimize recommendation performance.
Adaptive weighting would change the fixed-mixture hypothesis and require separate evaluation.

related_work.title: A Systematic Review and Replicability Study of BERT4Rec for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Identifies training duration and implementation efficiency as major confounders in BERT4Rec reproduction.
Motivates recording optimization trajectories, update counts and GPU cost.
limitations: Does not prescribe or validate the proposed three-arm experiment.
Released random-mask training differs from both the original explicit last-only mixture and potentially the corrected host sampler.

related_work.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss and autograd documentation
contributions: Defines mean reduction over nonignored targets, clarifying why pooled-target and per-sequence means differ.
Autograd-mode reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd; evaluation mode does not itself disable gradient computation.
limitations: Documentation defines implementation semantics rather than validating a recommendation objective.
The corrected baseline loss must be retained even if it is not cross-entropy.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled-ranking evaluation can differ from full-catalog conclusions.
Supports restricting claims to the pinned users, candidate construction and HR@10 protocol.
limitations: Does not authorize replacing the fixed host evaluator.
Does not remove checkpoint-selection optimism or training-seed uncertainty.
